reviews.text: Much like the satirical Network, Nightcrawler is the type of thriller that makes audiences think about things as the film moves along, frame by frame, into the Los Angeles underbelly late at night.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: A riveting, rich and masterfully assembled work of film noir, its gripping commentary and visuals are surpassed only by Gyllenhaal’s tremendous performance.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: The second half of this film is some of the most tense filmmaking I’ve seen in many years...
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: Indulge in the enigmatic charm of Gyllenhaal portraying an oddly likable sociopath, coupled with dark humor and a riveting yet straightforward plot. Nightcrawler isn't just a movie; it's a gift you give yourself, with a runtime that flies by.
reviews.author: John Flickinger

reviews.text: Although I was able to put aside my knowledge that nothing occurring in this film would happen in reality, there are moments in the film where I was pulled out of it...
reviews.author: Shadow and Act Staff

reviews.text: It’s such a creepy, tense, and efficient crime/psychological thriller.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Beneath Nightcrawler’s outward critique of the media’s desperate need to see and record human atrocity for mass ratings, there’s a more disturbing character study about Gyllenhaal’s fascinating and fantastically played psychopath.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is simply one of the best crime films of the 2010s.
reviews.author: Danilo Castro

reviews.text: In a knockout performance, Jake Gyllenhaal plays Louis Bloom, the type of guy who would not only sell his own mother but would chop her up into tiny pieces to facilitate the transaction.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Nightcrawler can be a hard film to stomach at times, but its message is sound. Outside of the strong craftsmanship, the film is a scarily magnetic character study of a guy who dreamed the American Dream in the absolute worst way possible.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: A razor's edge satire you'll be so busy being enthralled by you won't even notice the adrenaline shot of righteous anger being shot straight into your veins
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: There are a number of factors that contribute to the success of Nightcrawler ... but if ever a film were a one-man show, it is this one, as Gyllenhaal makes the movie his own from minute one.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal's transformation deserves an Oscar in one of this year's best films...
reviews.author: Dan Brightmore

reviews.text: Paints an ugly picture of the news business, but it's not simply a satire or condemnation. It's frequently funny and there are some very tense action scenes, but at the end it is Gyllenhaal's bold performance that stands out.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Thanks to Gyllenhaal's quirky and unhinged performance, this is a volatile ride worth taking.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: A pulse-pounding thriller set on the streets of Los Angeles, Nightcrawler stars a phenomenal Jake Gyllenhaal as a man who rises to fame by recording violent events in the middle of the night.
reviews.author: Film Companion Staff

reviews.text: Dan Gilroy's pitch black satire of the 24/7 news cycle and our morbid fascination with the misery of others is a devious delight.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: Bloom's vulture-like instincts and sense of ambition is symptomatic of a society that enjoys its breakfast cereal with a spoon of blood-tinged violence.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Just as we think things will snap into reality, Gilroy delves deeper into the surreal - working the satire with light taps to start, and ending with the thud of a hammer.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: It skilfully juggles a character with no redeeming features through his obsession with his work and thrusts him into a world where the lines between right and wrong are always questioned and debated.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is tense and intense, ferocious and obsessed, and crackles with energy and a dark sense of humor.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: As a whole, Nightcrawler is a flawed but fascinating film. Gyllenhaal's brilliant performance outweighs most of the faults in the rest of the movie.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is compelling and there is some truth in the way his character is able to elevate his status through sheer dogged determination and the demented zeal of a sociopath
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: 'Nightcrawler' is a clever thriller with a scoop that goes straight to the point. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: I really liked this movie... I found it a little dark.
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: I don't think my mom would like it, but that's fine. I did.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: It's an excitingly well written, dark hearted treatise with a vitriolic little statement all its own, a glorious new love letter to the seedy underside of Los Angeles, a city that bleeds during sleep.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's Lou Bloom may not have visible fangs, but he'd give any movie monster an authentic run for their money.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is an audacious mainstream thriller, a bombastic character study and a hell of a first movie for Gilroy, even if it's a little terrifying to think of what characters he will dream up next.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is Nightcrawler's battery; his creation, cooked from the greasy rinds of Jordan Belfort et al., saturates every frame with a queasy intensity.
reviews.author: Christopher Preston

reviews.text: The aphorisms scattered throughout the film allude to a larger truth. Sadly, the film's inability to empower these feeble social stabs with any authenticity or depth of investigation leaves events feeling flat and forgettable.
reviews.author: Patrick Gamble

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is a brilliantly-crafted Neo-noir that has a lingering effect long after the end credits. The film was deservedly nominated for an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Nightcrawler kept me on the edge of my seat and senses. It bleeds. It leads. And, you'll surely follow.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: A dark comedy and thriller rolled into one.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: It's a good performance from Gyllenhaal, and perhaps it's too good because he overshadows any of the social commentary with one of the year's most uncomfortable characters.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Nightcrawler attacked the mainstream media and the global financial crisis and the social inequities that create an undereducated class of internet-only consumers.
reviews.author: Tara Judah

reviews.text: The movie is a bit soulless, but that's the point.
reviews.author: Debbie Baldwin

reviews.text: A brisk pace, a taut story, and one hell of a vividly unnerving performance from Gyllenhaal; Dan Gilroy has crafted the most original thriller of the year. Nightcrawler will haunt you for days.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal's greasy performance as Lou Bloom is a spot-on psychopath, spewing forth banalities like a deranged creep, but he never goes so far as to make his character someone you don't recognize.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: Longtime screenwriter and first-time director Dan Gilroy loses some of the resonance when Bloom starts crossing lines, but there's another level of cultural relevance lurking in the characters.
reviews.author: Molly Templeton

reviews.text: As effective as it is as a character study, the action becomes flat out thrilling and suspenseful, and this is a fascinating, dark misadventure into a life driven by pure, pathetic ambition.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: Tense, atmospheric, chilling and always engaging, added to by a pulsating, frantic soundtrack, Nightcrawler is a special, often dark, film that strides over a minefield of morals.
reviews.author: Andrew Pollard

reviews.text: What a slick and thrilling vampire B-movie this is.
reviews.author: Camilla Long

reviews.text: ... a wicked satire of the tabloid news television that chases sensationalistic stories for ratings (the cliché "if it bleeds, it leads" is the guiding philosophy)
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal's performance is nothing short of legendary
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is tense and appalling, yet strangely funny, intriguing and engaging at the same time. Watch it.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: Nightcrawler [works] as a stylish and exciting thriller.
reviews.author: Rochelle Siemienowicz

reviews.text: This is a performance for the film history books, and one that Gyllenhaal inhabits totally.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: [Jake] Gyllenhaal is mesmerizing as the ruthlessly ambitious Bloom.
reviews.author: Brooke Corso

reviews.text: Most of all, Nightcrawler is a fine thriller and a great showcase for [Jake] Gyllenhaal's talent, wit, and comic timing.
reviews.author: Alex Heeney

reviews.text: Intriguing, unnerving and haunting.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Nightcrawler, on its surface, is a relatively straightforward thriller, built around a slightly improbable but very effective main character, a man who starts as an antihero and plunges straight ahead toward villainy.
reviews.author: Emily St. James

reviews.text: What's fascinating about this movie is the way in which writer/director Dan Gilroy treats Bloom. He's framed as a regular cinematic hero rather than a devious anti-hero.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Even if Gyllenhaal's Bloom doesn't entirely resonate, Nightcrawler is still an amusing, menacing and entertaining film.
reviews.author: Francesca Rudkin

reviews.text: "Lou Bloom" is one of the most memorable characters I've seen in years. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Sinister and upsetting and strangely magnetic - as the best movie monsters are - Gyllenhaal rises above the intermittently pedestrian screenplay.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Written crisply, directed unapologetically and acted brutally, Nightcrawler is one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Emine Yildirim

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's role overshadows the whole while also making it better.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: It's a small, compact, tightly written picture, shot in richly expressionist tones by Robert Elswit and guided by an exquisitely judged lead performance.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: For a movie that tries so hard to be disturbing, Nightcrawler is actually quite comforting. It takes a societal sickness and blames it on a boogeyman.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The fascinating, disturbing Nightcrawler questions the line between crime reportage, and reportage that's a crime in and of itself. That is, if that line still exists at all...
reviews.author: Kimberly Gadette

reviews.text: An emaciated Gyllenhaal plays Louis so adroitly, he must have been always intended to have this role. He snares the audience with his character's dark charm and floors you with his inhumanity.
reviews.author: Paul Chambers

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal is better than the sum of Nightcrawler's parts, but the film is still a riveting, horrific exploitation that blurs the lines between American greed and the American dream.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: A gripping drama about a wily hustler who finds success as a freelance photographer of night-time car crashes and violent crimes
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Nightcrawler gives us what we want--a "happy ending"-- as well as what we deserve-- a deliciously ironic comment on what passes for success in contemporary society.
reviews.author: Dan Jardine

reviews.text: "A chilling, addictive piece of pulp fiction driven full throttle by Gyllenhaal's revelatory performance."
reviews.author: Patrick Cooper

reviews.text: Nightcrawler feels like it's been building in Dan Gilroy for years. The director and his star have something interesting and even exciting on their hands. It's pretty can't miss stuff.
reviews.author: Blake Goble

reviews.text: Like an alternate version of Network in which Faye Dunaway cannibalizes the conscientious William Holden character, Nightcrawler cleverly dispenses with any debate about the tyranny of ratings and the erosion of privacy.
reviews.author: Joe Williams

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal, never one to shy away from the darkness of a character's soul, is absolutely in his element.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Although far from subtle, the metaphor of man as corporation is skillfully hidden behind black comedy, intense action and artful cinematography.
reviews.author: Donald Munro

reviews.text: Make no mistake, Nightcrawler is a major work for everyone involved.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: [Gyllenhaal's character] might be the post-recession cousin of Christian Bale in American Psycho. It's as if Humphrey Bogart had a baby face, lost all his marbles, and gotten a subscription to the Harvard Business Review.
reviews.author: Timothy Wainwright

reviews.text: Filmmaker Gilroy, brother to Tony (of the darkly marvellous Michael Clayton), makes every cinematic second count. If you blink you miss a tell-tale reaction shot, a vital visual plot clue, or a brilliant cut-in.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: It's a slinky black cat of a movie, commanding attention and reeling you in to follow down filthy, dangerous alleys.
reviews.author: Dave White

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal anchors Nightcrawler with a gonzo, transformative performance.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: Gilroy's script is less interested in social commentary than in crafting a slippery character study, and Gyllenhaal is perfectly suited to that.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: More a character study than a thriller, Nightcrawler is well-acted and compelling.
reviews.author: Edward Johnson-Ott

reviews.text: It's a modern-noir portrait of the way we eat our news, but amid the media, Nightcrawler slowly turns its unblinking eye on something darker. And much closer to home.
reviews.author: Genevieve Valentine

reviews.text: Writer-director Dan Gilroy create a compelling portrait of a slick hustler straight out of What Makes Sammy Run?, prowling the garish neon mean streets instead of the studios of Hollywood, willing to stoop to anything, even murder.
reviews.author: Jim Lane

reviews.text: As its title implies, writer-director Dan Gilroy's L.A. noir drama Nightcrawler will get under your skin with its profile of a go-getter whose ambition and amorality know no bounds.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: A gritty urban comedy noir, a scathing, Network-worthy disembowelment of television newsgatherers that will leave you craving a shower.
reviews.author: Scott Marks

reviews.text: It seems like a lot of satirical hue and cry about a social problem I'm not sure the nation is currently plagued by. Are local TV news stations really conducting daily bidding wars over the goriest footage random freelancers can bring them?
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: As befits a nightcrawler, this film suggests a creepy world of urban blight. Its rawness is as mesmerizing as it is threatening.
reviews.author: Mal Vincent

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal plays Louis, and he delivers a devil of a performance in one of the best movies of 2014.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: The film is as funny as it is unsettling... and it's plenty unsettling.
reviews.author: AP Kryza

reviews.text: Creepy, nasty, often hilarious stuff, Nightcrawler shows Gyllenhaal exactly where he seems to want to be and having the time of his life while he's at it.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: You never fail to keep your eyes glued to Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is a savvy story about the media's often compromised moral compass, built around a searing and indelible performance by the consistently impressive Jake Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: David Blaustein

reviews.text: When you throw in his passive aggressive personality, you've got one of the creepiest characters that we've seen on screen this year.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Headlined by career best work from Jake Gyllenhaal, Nightcrawler is one of the darker and craftier thrillers to come along in quite awhile.
reviews.author: Bill Clark

reviews.text: Stands apart from the crowd at the multiplex, a tight, absorbing thriller despite its rather murky messages.
reviews.author: Bruce Bennett

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's character isn't actually obsessed with real-life tragedy and carnage. Instead, his predatory creep has something else on his mind: success. Lou is a product of his generation - a DIY careerist, unburdened by a conscience.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: A true original, and a totally awesome entertainment, all the more so if you like your satire as bitter and black as a Turkish espresso.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: After all these years Jake Gyllenhaal has finally found his perfect role.
reviews.author: Luke Buckmaster

reviews.text: The film remains an amusingly sick joke and, despite its preachiness, a fun ride.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Working the space between the De Niros of 'Taxi Driver' and 'The King of Comedy,' Gyllenhaal is memorably creepy and almost cadaverous...
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Nightcrawler paints a pretty grim picture of modern society and the logical outcome of our collective insatiable thirst for information, bigger shocks and faster delivery.
reviews.author: Tim Martain

reviews.text: This is Gyllenhaal's film: his best since Zodiac, which it closely resembles.
reviews.author: Matt Glasby

reviews.text: When it comes to Nightcrawler, it is best to be both alert and alarmed.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Nightcrawler flourishes as a searing indictment on unchecked mania, workplace malpractice, and the forces that maintain them.
reviews.author: Colin Fraser

reviews.text: The film crackles with fetid electricity amid a strange nocturnal beauty.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: It's really an interesting film in a lot of ways and I was never bored but I also felt that it didn't really soar as much as I wanted it to.
reviews.author: Margaret Pomeranz

reviews.text: The noirish photography by Robert Elswit, best known for his work with Paul Thomas Anderson, is highly effective, making contemporary Los Angeles at night look nightmarish, and the performances are superb.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: Persuasive and smartly-scripted, Nightcrawler arrives at an interesting moment for Hollywood cinema.
reviews.author: Shane Danielsen

reviews.text: Glides out of the darkness and seizes you by the throat.
reviews.author: Tom Clift

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhall gets his Rupert Pupkin on in Nightcrawler, the heir apparent to Martin Scorsese's own satire of media infamy and celebrity (at any cost), The King of Comedy.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: The fact Gyllenhaal holds our attention and our care for so much of this film is an achievement but also strangely terrifying.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: [F]eaturing one who lurks at night to gather crime footage for broadcast, the film parodies the obsession (with taking images) and notes it to be a tragedy of our times.
reviews.author: Matthew Sorrento

reviews.text: ...a passable effort that boasts a seriously above-average central performance.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The most cynical journalism movie in years. Shows us a troubled young man with a scuzzy air about him, with little in the way of education or social graces, who may in fact be a full-on sociopath, and concludes, "that guy should be a TV journalist!"
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: It's a no-nonsense, old-school exercise, with a tinge of borderline trashiness.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is artful and frighteningly plausible.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: The anti-hero wacko is played to the hilt by Jake Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal's 'nightcrawling' TV cameraman drags ambulance-chasing to a new low in this disturbing tale of a creepy sociopath feeding TV's blood-thirst for the goriest footage.
reviews.author: Tim Evans

reviews.text: The film embodies the dark night of the main character's soul as well as our own.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: ... the best Martin Scorsese movie not directed by Scorsese. It's that good, that assured ... that unshakable ... Scores as both urban thriller and 'Network'-like comment on the media.
reviews.author: Glenn Lovell

reviews.text: ...a fascinating character study with a riveting and utterly creepy performance by Jake Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: Despite the grisly trimmings and Gyllenhaal's unhinged performance, it's coldly analytical and dry as a bone.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: The greatest range of topography, however, plays over the gaunt features of Jake Gyllenhaal, eyes wide, nearly unblinking, cheekbones like a hungry wolf. His Lou Bloom is a lone wolf, too, a nattering autodidact...
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: A slick and nightmarish descent into a world where corporate justice rewards those who do whatever it takes to get ahead. It's more than fitting that this horror show of American capitalism opened on Halloween .
reviews.author: Jeff Meyers

reviews.text: The film, at one level, is a screeching indictment of the American appetite, far more voracious than our own, for small-scale human suffering at the top of local news bulletins.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: A thoroughly captivating film you can't easily shake off.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is creepy in his best screen performance yet
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: First-time director Dan Gilroy maintains a good pace throughout the film. It works on every level as drama, social commentary, action. The cinematography by Oscar-winner Robert Elswit is excellent.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Crashes and crime scenes are his bread and butter. He is driven. He is innovative. He is happy. He is also a monster - a fiend who preys on people at their weakest and worst moments.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Gilroy's directorial debut is a crazy cool indictment of media voyeurism from which you'll be powerless to look away.
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: A hypnotic confluence of action, comedy and hysteria that is at once unnerving, exhilarating and unlike anything I've ever seen.
reviews.author: Sam Fragoso

reviews.text: A fascinating study of what humans are capable of when logic overruns the conscience.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: It's alternately terrifying and spellbinding to watch the action unfold, through a climactic street scene that had me on the edge of my seat.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: Gilroy is so plugged into his antihero's grotesque opportunism that it's hard not to feel a residual kick.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: A messy but intriguing and enjoyably warped slice of modern film noir as only Los Angeles can flavor it.
reviews.author: Gary Dowell

reviews.text: Nightcrawler sends its media criticism out in ALL CAPS, bludgeoning Jake Gyllenhaal's excellent performance.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: Noirish 1950s cynicism meets nasty 1970s Corman-esque exploitation in a thriller that is uncomfortable, unpleasant, unforgiving, and pretty darn brilliant.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: A riveting character study, but also an unsettling look at what the economy is doing to us as a society.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal haunts Nightcrawler like a ghost who's seen a ghost...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: If you squint you can see this film as a satire, but then that betrays what a fantastic, atmospheric thriller "Nightcrawler" is at heart.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal impresses as a sociopathic news hound.
reviews.author: Scott Nash

reviews.text: A well crafted, relentlessly discomforting and disturbing, psychologically dense thriller. But would you trust say, the NSA to police itself? Namely, a hit list here of small screen competition and annoying paparazzi. Omission Alert, just sayin' is all.
reviews.author: Prairie Miller

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal has done a magnificent job transforming himself inwards, thinning out those film star looks until he resembles an unmasked Scooby Doo villain.
reviews.author: Ali Gray

reviews.text: Part scathing media satire, part scorching crime thriller.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: A sobering cautionary tale suggesting that you reflect upon all the motivations of a news source before swallowing the veracity of a story, hook, line and sinker.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: Now 33 years old, Gyllenhaal is the same age that De Niro was in Taxi Driver and, like him, he is learning to channel an eerie, inner charisma, offering it up in glimpses and glimmers rather than all at once.
reviews.author: Christopher Orr

reviews.text: For a first-time director, Gilroy demonstrates an uncommon assurance, not only in his audacious tonal shifts but in the stellar work he elicits from his cast and crew.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: It grows more and more preposterous but it never loosens its grip thanks to a riveting Mr. Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Barbara Vancheri

reviews.text: A mesmerizing cipher, Lou is a spiritual descendant of Robert De Niro's Travis Bickle in Taxi Driver, and of the withholding protagonists in the existential French crime films of Robert Bresson and Jean-Pierre Melville
reviews.author: Richard Corliss

reviews.text: Anchored by Jake Gyllenhaal's chilling performance, Nightcrawler is an effective neo-noir thriller that provides insightful social commentary on the side.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: You can't stop watching the demented, sociopathic, narcissistic but refreshingly blunt Jake Gyllenhaal in the razor-sharply written and visually exquisite "Nightcrawler".
reviews.author: Adam Fendelman

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal delivers a terrifically unsettling performance.
reviews.author: Clint O'Connor

reviews.text: The ultimate trick or treat: a scathing satire dressed up as a noir thriller.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: After a few minutes you know everything about Louis you're going to know; the only surprise in Nightcrawler is the level of grotesqueness it achieves.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: This dark satirical thriller develops some suspense with a character-driven approach.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: It isn't a perfect movie, not by any stretch, but it's without question the role that will coax you on the Gyllenhaal bandwagon if you weren't there already.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: With 'Nightcrawler,' Jake Gyllenhaal adds to his latest round of extreme characterizations with another superior performance here.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: A worthy addition to landmark tales of journalistic ethics such as the Kirk Douglas classic Ace In The Hole and the Oscar-winning Network.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: Nightcrawler would be worth seeing for Jake Gyllenhaal's performance alone, but it's also a gripping and entertaining deep-dive into a nocturnal world of ruthless opportunism as well as a deliciously caustic satire on moral responsibility.
reviews.author: Catherine Bray

reviews.text: With such a dysfunctional, amoral protagonist, Nightcrawler should be difficult to fully embrace, but Gyllenhaal and writer/director Dan Gilroy expertly toy with our sympathies.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Whether it is just coincidence that Bloom's character fits Gyllenhaal like a glove, or whether it is testimony to his profound acting skill, he takes his role, and what otherwise would have been a lightweight film, to dizzying heights.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: [Gilroy] wants Louis, who perpetrates some ghastly escapades, to epitomize the sick soul of media exploitation, but he also celebrates him as an entrepreneurial go-getter who is just giving us hypocrites what we secretly (or not-so-secretly) crave.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Howard's intrusive score enhances the sense that Nightcrawler is a movie and nothing more. Which is fine, of course. But the movie's movie-ness makes you aware that a statement is being made without articulating what it is.
reviews.author: Wesley Morris

reviews.text: Nightcrawler deliberately blurs the lines between David Cronenberg-like satire, crime thriller and horror. It also poses as a twisted version of the traditional story about the all-American entrepreneur, trying to get ahead any way he can.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: It's hard not to be fascinated by the dark places Gyllenhaal goes here. But "Nightcrawler" falls short as social commentary or even psychological yarn. Like Louis, it talks a good game that crumbles as you ponder it.
reviews.author: Lisa Kennedy

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is a scathing Network-like satire dressed as a creepy thriller.
reviews.author: Kirk Baird

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal, in a disturbing humdinger of a performance, plays Louis Bloom, a would-be news cameraman whose lack of conscience and rabid ambition make him brilliant at his chosen career.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: ...tightly written and directed by Dan Gilroy, Jake Gyllenhaal gives a tour de force...buttressed by atmospheric cinematography and tension-enhancing music. It is also an homage to Los Angeles with 75 different locations.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Perhaps the only thing more disturbing than Jake Gyllenhaal's performance as a borderline personality with a camcorder is the nauseating sensation that we almost like Louis Bloom.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's magnetic performance is center stage.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Lou Bloom is a cross between Nosferatu and Ed Grimley.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: It's a 21st-century takedown of the media's pandering ''if it bleeds, it leads'' ethos and the ghoulish nightcrawlers who live by it.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: This is a classic film, not just because every scene and line is casually beautiful and devoid of extraneous touches, but because its tone is mercilessly exact.
reviews.author: Matt Zoller Seitz

reviews.text: As an LA myth from the school of Michael Mann, Nightcrawler works quite brilliantly.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal gives one of the year's best performances in a very well-done, intense thriller that looks at TV news from a bottom-feeding viewpoint.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: A gently comical undertone makes this thriller even creepier than expected, bolstered by sharp writing and directing from Dan Giloy and an especially clever performance from Jake Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: You will laugh at Nightcrawler, but mostly out of discomfort, and when you do, your laughter will catch in your throat.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: The good-to-see Rene Russo plays the ratings-happy producer showing off Bloom's wares on a nightly basis, but this is strictly the often chilling Gyllenhaal's one-man show.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: A rousing and visionary piece of work...a kinetic joyride that surfs a giddy wave of dark wit and intelligence..deserves to be mentioned in same sentence as Network.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: Writer/director Dan Gilroy goes for the jugular in his insanely entertaining, disturbing indictment of the media from its insensitivity towards victims to far darker charges. And that's only "Nightcrawler's" surface agenda...
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Trains a searchlight on the TV news business, and flushes out some of its creepiest denizens.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Lou might as well be a 21st Century Travis Bickle, and Gyllenhaal seems to be having fun channeling his inner Robert De Niro.
reviews.author: Willie Waffle

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal is focused, intense and terrifying.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal delivers on the promise he showed nine years ago in Ang Lee's Brokeback Mountain.
reviews.author: David Edwards

reviews.text: ...cleverly always keeps fear somewhere in the frame.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: A movie for the pleasure of movie audiences pretending to be shocked by a story of ghoulish media.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: The nightmares that Bloom is selling are immaterial; what terrifies more is the cut-throat corporate culture that so willingly pays him - and pats him on the back.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: 'Nightcrawler' manages to be a scathing look at ambition and journalistic sensationalism while still delivering as a dark thriller.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: Nightcrawler savages the news media's ratings-driven ethic (a most unethical ethic) with such force, it brings to mind Paddy Chayefsky and Sidney Lumet's Network.
reviews.author: Tirdad Derakhshani

reviews.text: A horror movie for anyone who's survived layoffs and pay cuts and been told to "work smarter."
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Credit writer/director Dan Gilroy for taking a shot with an unpleasant lead character and his business of pure ugliness, pulling off an amazing filmmaking achievement with this devious but hypnotic effort.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The nearly two hour long movie is a wild ride, particularly as fueled by Gyllenhaal's edgy, nuanced, and completely mesmerizing performance. (Complete Content Review for Parents also available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: It's a cross between "Network" and "Silence of the Lambs."
reviews.author: John Hanlon

reviews.text: "Nightcrawler" executes its ideas with tremendous craft and cool, and the courageous and counterintuitive pairing of its leads - Russo is 60, and Gyllenhaal 33 - produces two electrical, interlocking performances and undeniable erotic chemistry.
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: This isn't fun, escapist entertainment but, when it works, it's fascinating and compelling and makes us take a hard look at what TV news is selling and where it's getting the product.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is a thrilling, dark journey into the mind of a sociopath and the cutthroat nature of success at all costs. It taps into that lurid vein of morbid fascination.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal may well earn himself at least an Oscar nomination for the role, but credit must go to veteran screenwriter and first-time director Dan Gilroy, who has created a wholly unique and absolutely disturbing vision.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: [Gyllenhall] is hypnotic and electrifying as the skull-like Louis Bloom, a strange man in need of steady work who hurls himself into the high-speed, extremely competitive world of "nightcrawlers."
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: A smart, engaged film powered by an altogether remarkable performance by Jake Gyllenhaal, it is melodrama grounded in a disturbing reality, an extreme scenario that is troubling because it cuts close to the bone.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: A thrilling and superbly acted picture which immediately identifies itself as an example of cult cinema whilst never sacrificing its chilling substance over its vast amount of style.
reviews.author: Jon Lyus

reviews.text: Like the ending or not, the film finds strength in the performances by Gyllenhaal and Russo. Their work is as captivating to watch as a police chase on a Los Angeles freeway.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: It's a solid first time out in any event, entertainingly obvious at some points, obvious-obvious at others, and jazzed to have a rich subject and a star willing to run with it.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal gives the best performance of his career in this gripping LA drama from screenwriter-turned-director Dan Gilroy.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Nightcrawler serves as a phenomenal showcase for Gyllenhaal, who is never less than riveting . A full package of tics, tension and breathless patter, this self-taught entrepreneur stops at nothing, evoking a Taxi Driver for the TMZ age.
reviews.author: Preston Jones

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal gives what may be the best performance of his career.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Absolutely intense, a fantastic debut by Dan Gilroy with Gyllenhaal giving an unforgettable performance that shows him achieving the next level as an actor.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: It would be comforting to be able to see Nightcrawler as satire ... That would be very comforting, indeed.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Writer-director Dan Gilroy wants it both ways - snarling comedy and gripping thriller - and for the most part he gets what he wants.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: For his directing debut, Gilroy is out for the contact high of that Mean Streets vibe, and Gyllenhaal and Russo deliver it to him in spades.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal is mesmerizing as the MacGyver of masturbatory shut-in Googlers, Oswald Cobblepot with Pat Riley hair, raised in a crawlspace on Robert Kiyosaki books.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: The way [Gyllenhaal] toggles between empty stares and blabbermouthed 'charm' when confronting his prey is reminiscent of no less than Scarlett Johnasson in 'Under the Skin.'
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: An indictment of the American workplace and a piercing character study.
reviews.author: Jon Niccum

reviews.text: Nightcrawler doesn't err cautiously but on the side of discomfort, and you have to admire that.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: Dan Gilroy's "Nightcrawler" is a dark dream of a thriller, full of evil that floats like a toxic cloud across an already tainted city.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: True to its title, creeps under the viewer's skin much like the predatory title character, who restlessly cruises through this modern-day media allegory like Travis Bickle's long-lost, hyper-wired West Coast cousin.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: One of the year's most satisfying and original thrillers.
reviews.author: Kristin Tillotson

reviews.text: No matter how extreme or unlikely the scenario, we want to know how Lou will handle it. Gyllenhaal makes this antihero funny, scary and fearlessly strange.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Weitzman

reviews.text: Nightcrawler curves and hisses its way into your head with demonic skill. This is a deliciously twisted piece of work. And Gyllenhaal, coiled and ready to spring, is scarily brilliant.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Wants to be cutting-edge, but in the end its creative blade proves rather dull. Still, it's hard to take your eyes off Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: That Gyllenhaal totally commits to Lou can't be questioned. The actor seamlessly embodies this strange and scary man, finding ways to turn his fidgety tics and baleful glances into reams of telling information.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: There are moments that are too macabre and outlandish, but Gilroy steers the movie just this side of farce, just this side of Chayefsky, and keeps it all within a realistic framework.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: "Nightcrawler" is the kind of movie that rarely hits multiplexes anymore, an edgy, pulpy thriller with a social conscience and a vicious satirical streak.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal delivers his best performance to date.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Has little new to say about its subject but nonetheless thrives courtesy of its seedy, nocturnal L.A. atmosphere and a magnetic, uninhibited lead performance by Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: "Jon Stewart could learn a thing from Gilroy's rightly ruthless excoriation."
reviews.author: Inkoo Kang

reviews.text: It's great, wicked fun.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Sharp, dark, satirical and bone-rattlingly thrilling, with a career-peak turn from Jake Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Dan Jolin

reviews.text: Nightcrawler features the craziest, creepiest, coolest sonofabitch Jake Gyllenhaal has played on screen yet.
reviews.author: Chase Whale

reviews.text: A monster movie for the modern age.
reviews.author: Adam Woodward

reviews.text: Director Gilroy, the scriptwriter of Bourne Legacy, may not be ripping the lid off shady newsgathering, but he has crafted a film that is properly creepy.
reviews.author: Siobhan Synnot

reviews.text: Skin crawling stuff.
reviews.author: Josh Slater-Williams

reviews.text: A truly exceptional thriller highlighted by a wickedly entrancing, career-best performance from Jake Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: Both main performances are hand-in-glove terrific, with Russo id to Gyllenhaal's ego.
reviews.author: Duane Dudek

reviews.text: A compelling and altogether impressive directorial debut for screenwriter Dan Gilroy
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: A modest and effectively executed urban thriller, suspenseful and entertaining in its clammy, overwrought way.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's not afraid to go creeper on his audience and leave them uneasy about what he'll do next. It's movie acting at a high level ...
reviews.author: Jeff Baker

reviews.text: If you're ever trying to think of an actor who's carved out an interesting career for himself and doesn't get due credit, here's your answer.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Despite the familiarity of its themes ... Gilroy's clever, skeezy little noir is worth a prowl.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is well worth seeing just for Gyllenhaal's spectacularly creepy performance.
reviews.author: Mike D'Angelo

reviews.text: A thick film of sleaze coats every frame of "Nightcrawler," a movie that takes a hard look at media culture and provides Jake Gyllenhaal a terrific opportunity to creep us all out.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Thirty pounds lighter, all cheekbones and bulging eyes, Gyllenhaal plays one of the year's most memorable characters in this dark, provocative drama.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: The drama feels heightened and overwrought, and yet it works; you can see Nina's cold-eyed desperation, and Lou's creepy rapture as he realizes that he can get a shot that nobody else has.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: A grim, gruesome, gripping thriller that gets funnier and nastier in equal measures.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is Intensely Enthralling throughout this film.
reviews.author: Diana Saenger

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is the culmination of everything Gyllenhaal has been building to since setting off on a different path.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: This smart thriller-drama has dark gravity and a sharp-toothed smile, with Jake Gyllenhaal giving one of 2014's best performances in an economic horror film that oozes through the L.A. night.
reviews.author: James Rocchi

reviews.text: Lou epitomizes all-American ambition left to curdle in the media spotlight, the extent to which he is willing to endanger others coming to a head in a nerve-wracking finale.
reviews.author: William Goss

reviews.text: You see some influence of other iconic characters - Norman Bates, Verbal Kint, Gordon Gekko - but Gyllenhaal's Lou Bloom becomes his own icon.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: It ultimately proves questionable and unconvincing, but in this case, failure to launch is noble. It keeps you creeped out and fascinated.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Dark and cynical, filled with savage, scathing commentary about our media's relentless exploitation of violence.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: In real life, nobody could obstruct as much justice as Louis does and get away with it. Still, Nightcrawler is unnerving because we never know just how far Louis will go.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: [VIDEO ESSAY] Jake Gyllenhaal's canny portrayal delivers a revelatory character study of an opportunistic sociopath working all the angles in a system built on propaganda.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Dan Gilroy's directorial debut only offers a familiar vision of today's newsman and producers as misery peddlers, and callow ratings slaves bordering on the monstrous.
reviews.author: Chris Cabin

reviews.text: The hypnotic electronic score from James Newton Howard and neon-tinged vision of LA from Roger Elswitt recall Drive, but there's none of that film's wistful abandon here.
reviews.author: Emma Dibdin

reviews.text: Dan Gilroy's sleek and slick indictment of TV news crawls under the skin thanks, in great part, to a knockout performance from a sensational Jake Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Debut director Dan Gilroy has crafted a characterful satire that doesn't say much that's original but which skewers its targets with humour and flair.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Switch off that television and head out to the cinema: Gyllenhaal is sensational headlining a pitch-black satire with its finger on the pulse.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: It scuttles ahead, wide-eyed, antennae waving, on a journey to the end of the night, and toward a future when nothing will not be shown.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Apparently we won't stop enabling the MEDIA to sell us fear, so maybe getting to know the people who deliver it will help.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: From the distance, it can look like the mutated cousin of something like "Broadcast News" or "Network." When you come in closer, you'll see something semi-fresh but ultimately quite defective.
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: This is a terrific performance by Gyllenhaal, completely inhabiting a spook of a man, a ghoul to remember.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: In director Dan Gilroy's sleek crime-thriller, Jake Gyllenhaal has found a role in which he can act against his good looks and buff bod. He throws himself out there and falls - until something darker and deeper kicks in.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: The wildly evocative film proves there's a Lou Bloom lurking inside most of us. He's just the one willing to cross the yellow police tape.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: It holds a mirror up to a major city in a modern time, but introduces a psychotic, sociopathic tour guide who instantly becomes one for the ages.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: There's not an ounce of fat on the film. It gets in, it tells the story as well as it possibly can, and it cuts out perfectly.
reviews.author: Drew McWeeny

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal pushes himself even further as the unforgettable Lou Bloom, a sociopath with a pretty solid business plan who taps into a vein of darkness in Los Angeles that proves a profitable one.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: First and foremost, the film is a showcase for its wiry and wired star, and for the fascinatingly amoral anti-hero he brings to life.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: A thought-provoking and strangely hilarious feature that blends elements of drama and horror with the blackest of comedy, Nightcrawler is a film that truly gets under the skin.
reviews.author: Chris Tilly

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal, who summons career-best work, simply couldn't have played this character a few years ago.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: Try to imagine the acrid TV satire of Network, lit up by the sodium glare of an LA crime flick from the 1980s, and you're some of the way into Nightcrawler.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Like his erratic protagonist, Gilroy doesn't always know when to settle down or call it quits, and the film's constant shifts of tone can grow tiring, even if the action as a whole never gets boring.
reviews.author: Jordan Mintzer

reviews.text: Dan Gilroy's tonally bold directorial debut can't quite pull together its differing ambitions, resulting in a story that's not entirely satisfying as a dark character study, amoral thriller or curt commentary on the sensationalism of local TV news.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: A feast of capital-A acting that's sometimes amusing to watch but not believable for so much as a second.
reviews.author: Scott Foundas

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's performance is so dedicated, and Gilroy's world so determinedly realised that it forces its way to originality.
reviews.author: Henry Barnes

reviews.text: If Billy Wilder's 'Ace in the Hole' and 'Network' had a mutant baby, it would probably look like Dan Gilroy's 'Nightcrawler'
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: Nightcrawler is a fresh, brilliantly led crime thriller that's coated with just enough sleaze to ease consumption, and upset digestion.
reviews.author: Sam Woolf

reviews.text: A fantastic, sleek and fun satire.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: A full-on masterpiece. Darkly funny, frightening, and action-packed. An intriguing neo-noir take on a world most of us are happily oblivious to.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Deliciously macabre... Nightcrawler is popcorn snuff.
reviews.author: Brian Formo

reviews.text: Deeply philosophical while remaining both captivating and entertaining, Nightcrawler is that rare breed of worm, one with an Art Film heart and a Hollywood shine...Easily one of this year's best films.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: A deliciously dark, cynical and riveting examination of struggle and suffering gone awry.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

synopsis: Los Angeles denizen Louis Bloom (Jake Gyllenhaal) survives by scavenging and petty theft. He stumbles into a new career as a cameraman and -- armed with a camcorder and police scanner -- begins nocturnal forays across the city in search of shocking and grisly crimes. When he catches the eye of a shopworn news director (Rene Russo) who welcomes the chance to raise her station's ratings, Louis goes to increasingly greater lengths to catch the "money shot."
